name: screen_gf
headline: GF: among 326 candidate types (17 in-silico hits at >= 5 Hz), connectome-guided ranking finds the first hit after 1.0 experiments vs 18.2 expected for random order (18.17x; other >=2-hop score variants 18.17-18.17x; naive 'largest type first' order: 3.0) and all hits after 317.0 vs 308.8 (0.97x; other >=2-hop variants 1.02-1.1x); exhaustive = 326 experiments. With a budget of 20 experiments (6% of the screen) the guided order finds 14/17 hits vs 1.0 expected for random order. Second-seed replicate: 16/17 hits replicate; all robust hits found after 295.0 vs 307.8 random (1.04x).
literature_headline: Literature check: the guided order reaches the first literature-known driver of GF (LPLC2, connectome rank 2; set: LPLC2, LC4) after 2.0 experiments vs 109.0 expected random (54.5x; direct-synapse-only ranking: 1.0); in-silico recall of literature hits 2/2.

definitions.hit: mean firing rate of the GF group >= 5 Hz when all neurons of the candidate type are driven with Poisson input at 150 Hz (2 trials x 500 ms). Model baseline is 0 Hz, so any firing is evoked. Threshold chosen by us before the full screen (not externally pre-registered); sensitivity in 'sensitivity_threshold', seed replicate in 'seed_robustness'.
definitions.experiment: one whole-brain LIF simulation (flylab.brain.simulate) activating one candidate cell type
definitions.connectome_score: see flylab.screen.rank_by_connectome docstring. meanfield = predicted mean depolarisation (mV, threshold 7 mV) of the target neurons from (max_hops-1) fixed-point steps of the brain model's own LIF mean-field equations (no fitted parameters); fraction = direct signed input fraction + normalised multi-hop excitatory paths
definitions.random_baseline: exact expectation over uniformly random test orders, not a sampled run

brain_params.model: LIF after Shiu et al. 2024 (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07763-9), FlyWire v783

ranking.ranking_note: matrix_build_s is a one-time cost (sparse connectome matrices), included in the guided wall time; ranking all candidates afterwards takes ranking_s

guided.tie_note: primary numbers are tie-aware expectations (candidates with equal score tested in random order); 'deterministic' breaks ties alphabetically

random.formula: first hit: (N+1)/(K+1); all hits: K(N+1)/(K+1) (exact expectations over all orders)
random.p_note: P(random order finds >= 1 hit within floor(guided experiments_to_first_hit)) = 1 - C(N-K,k)/C(N,k)

discovery_curve.note: cumulative hits found after k experiments (guided = deterministic order; random = exact expectation k*K/N)

largest_type_first.note: order by number of neurons in the type (desc), no connectome; ties tested in random order. A stronger baseline than random: larger types inject more spikes, so they are more likely to drive anything.

seed_robustness.note: every candidate with target rate >= 2.5 Hz (seed 0) re-simulated with seed 1; candidates below that are assumed non-hits. robust hit = hit in both seeds.

evidence.why: LPLC2 necessary for GF-mediated escape (Ache 2019); activation -> jumping (Wu 2016)
LC4 activation -> jumping (Wu 2016); LC4 synapses directly onto the GF and conveys looming velocity (Ache 2019 abstract; von Reyn 2017). Jumping was not shown to be GF-mediated

literature.precision: not computable: literature negatives are unknown for most of the candidate types; lower bound = literature-known fraction of in-silico hits

random.p_note: P(random order finds >= 1 hit within floor(guided experiments_to_first_hit)) = 1 - C(N-K,k)/C(N,k)

novel_in_silico_hits.note: agent-generated hypotheses: in-silico hits not among the literature-known hits used here (incl. extra_sets) - may be known elsewhere, or model artefacts; untested

timing.cache_note: per-experiment wall times are the measured simulation times (also for rows replayed from spikes/screen/out/screen_cache.jsonl); wall_s_benchmark_total is this run's own wall time and is small when the screen is replayed from the cache
timing.hardware_note: shared 16-thread Windows laptop CPU, 2 threads per experiment, other jobs running

limitations: In-silico ground truth uses the same connectome as the ranking (partly circular); literature agreement is the independent check, and it covers only a few known hits.
Literature negatives are unknown, so precision vs biology cannot be computed.
All neurons of a type are activated at one Poisson rate; split-GAL4 lines label subsets with unknown rates.
Model has no spontaneous activity, no neuromodulation, no plasticity; only firing of the target group is read out (not behaviour).
Wall times are for this shared machine; the speed-up in experiment counts is hardware independent.

Score choice: the primary score (meanfield, 3 hops) was chosen after a rank-only check showed that 2-hop scores miss LC16 -> MDN, whose MDN drive we had seen in a 6-type pilot simulation. The contract's input-fraction score and all hop counts are reported in 'sensitivity_score_variants'; the first-hit speed-up is robust across >= 2-hop variants, the all-hits speed-up is not (see there).
The hit threshold (5 Hz mean target rate) is a convention; see 'sensitivity_threshold'.

Hits near the threshold depend on the random seed (2 trials x 500 ms; the GF group has 2 neurons, so the mean-rate resolution is 0.5 Hz); see 'seed_robustness' for which hits replicate with a second seed.

Random order is a weak baseline; 'baselines.largest_type_first' (no connectome, bigger types first) is a stronger one and also beats random, so only part of the speed-up is due to connectome structure.
